rationale: Author-of-record, round 2, re-derived against git show 99d75484 plus the resulting tree — never the fix report. My single round-1 concrete ask (G4, the plan-listed crashed-holder recovery test) is ADDRESSED: TestPhaseLock_CrashedHolderReleases_Unix is a REAL subprocess test (os.Args[0] re-exec with an env-guarded helper, marker-file held-handshake, SIGKILL while holding, process reaped via Wait, then reacquisition asserted to succeed in under one second against a 2s bound), and the Windows leg takes exactly the disclosed-argued-deviation path my ask offered as the alternative: the doc comments (phaselock_test.go and phaselock_windows_errors.go) state the argument — no Windows CI runner exists, LockFileEx crashed-holder release is documented Win32 kernel semantics rather than this package's code, and the package's own Windows-specific logic (retry classification) is seam-extracted constraint-free and tested on every platform. That is an honest disposition, reviewable and reviewed. Whole-bead re-judgment: the fn signature's second change to (stored string, present bool) is the forced consequence of G1's presence-aware read and I judge it acceptable under the same reasoning as round-1 deviation A — readPhaseForLock's three-way split (lookup failure propagates pre-fn; present-but-invalid never converts to absence; only genuinely-absent backfills) is precisely what the panel demanded, and deliberately NOT retrofitted onto readStoredPhaseWithCache's widely-depended-on read-only contract. Values remain GENUINELY unchanged at all nine wrap sites (re-read every closure: plan 'implement', spec 'plan', complete nextMode, release mode, impl Derived and done+mindspec_done, adopt's audit map, migrate's backfill pair, repair's derived-under-guard); the two sync writers are still best-effort by design but now surface failures via DescribeLockFailure with the ADR-0035 never-delete treatment. repair now derives INSIDE the critical section with a fresh per-call Cache, closing the fresh-stored-vs-stale-target asymmetry and matching spec.md:113's pinned read->derive->compare->write mechanism; AC-5(v)'s final-stored-review assertion survives the barrier rework. The fence still has exactly zero production callers of SanctionedDerivedSync (re-grepped), which now propagates a failed children read — the hard-block driver — instead of deriving from a nil slice. The ripple changes are honest adaptations, not gate-weakening: the adopt/impl test stubs ADD the bd-show fixture wiring the now-stricter (fails-closed) production path requires, with comments saying exactly why; the raw-ID-render ratchet recounts 5->1 and 3->1 are arithmetically verified — the old function had exactly 5 raw-epicID and 3 raw-specID Sprintf sites, and the rework REPLACED all but one of each with idrender-wrapped renders inside the closure, so the counts dropped because raw sites were eliminated (a strengthening), and the updated Gate text narrates precisely that. Scope discipline holds: every new surface (DescribeLockFailure, SetLockWaitForTest, readPhaseForLock, repairFindRootFn, releaseSyncPhase/completeSyncPhase, shouldRetryWindowsLockError) traces to a consolidated group G1-G8; nothing beyond the panel's asks was touched. Empirical: go build green; internal/phase green under -race (crashed-holder test included); cmd/mindspec, internal/approve, internal/complete, internal/lint, internal/guard all green -short from the bead worktree; NO stray phase.lock in the bead worktree, the spec worktree, or the main checkout after the runs (round 1's G2 failure mode did not recur); bead worktree left byte-identical. Two advisory residuals recorded in findings; neither gates.

findings.detail: TestPhaseLock_CrashedHolderReleases_Unix (internal/phase/phaselock_test.go:111) delivers the plan step-2 unix leg for real: a subprocess re-exec of the test binary acquires the lock at a fixture path, signals via a marker file only AFTER acquisition, hangs on a sleep (deliberately not select{} — the doc comment even explains Go's deadlock detector would self-terminate the sole goroutine), is SIGKILLed, reaped with Wait, and the parent's next acquirePhaseFileLock is asserted to succeed in under a second. The Windows-leg disposition is the argued-deviation alternative my round-1 ask explicitly offered: disclosed in two doc comments with the argument stated (no Windows CI runner; crashed-holder release is documented Win32 kernel semantics, not package code; the package's own Windows logic — the retry classification — is extracted into constraint-free phaselock_windows_errors.go and tested cross-platform, ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION-only). The silent-absence defect is cured; what remains untested is a platform-semantics claim, honestly labeled as such.

findings.assessment: Signature change to func(stored string, present bool): acceptable, same grounds as round-1 deviation A.
findings.detail: The presence bit is the minimal carrier for G1's absent-vs-invalid distinction; readPhaseForLock's stricter contract is correctly kept SEPARATE from readStoredPhaseWithCache (whose collapse-to-empty contract many read-only derivation callers depend on — changing it would have been genuine scope creep). All nine call sites adapted mechanically; only migrate.go actually consumes the bit, and its present-but-invalid-never-backfilled semantics (repair is the lever for corruption, not a silent backfill) is the right division of authority. The AC-5(vi) walker's anchor is unaffected. Bead 2's consumers get a shape that already distinguishes the states EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 will need.
